# Pin Input

A fixed-length code entered into one input drawn as boxes — one-time codes and PINs.

```tsx
import { PinInput } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `pin-input` |
| Family | inputs |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | `field`, `visually-hidden` |

## Behavior

A single labelled text input, capped at `length`, rendered as a row of boxes it lies over. Composed with Field for the label, helper text and validation. Autofill, paste and Backspace are the platform's, because there is only one input.

Headless contract: `getPinInputProps` in `packages/primitives/src/pin-input.ts` — importable from `@rata/primitives` without the React wrapper or any CSS.

- **One input, with the boxes drawn — never one input per box** — Six inputs is how most code fields are built and it breaks four things at once: SMS and email autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) fills one input, not six; paste lands in the first box only unless every box intercepts it; a screen reader announces six unlabelled edit fields; and Backspace across boxes has to be reimplemented and is usually wrong at the boundaries. One input gets all four from the platform. The boxes are an `aria-hidden` rendering of its value, with the caret position drawn as the active box.
- **No APG pattern applies, so it is a text input and says so** — There is no WAI-ARIA pattern for a segmented code, and inventing a composite role would announce something no reader has learned. It is a labelled `textbox` with `maxLength`, `inputmode` and `autocomplete` — which is what it is.
- **`purpose` rather than a `mask` boolean** — Masking is a consequence of what the code is, and so are autofill and the input type. A one-time code is something the reader is copying from elsewhere: it should be visible and fillable. A PIN is a secret: it should be masked and never suggested. A `mask` boolean would let someone build a visible PIN or a masked one-time code, and both are wrong.
- **`onComplete` does not submit the form** — Auto-advancing when the last character lands is the reason the component exists, so the hook is there. Submitting a form on the reader's behalf is a different act: it fires on a paste that was the wrong code, and it is unrecoverable if the next screen is a navigation. The caller starts verification; the reader stays on the field until it passes, and a failure clears the value and keeps focus.
- **Length is stated, not only drawn** — The boxes tell a sighted reader how long the code is. A screen-reader user hears none of them, so the count joins the description chain from the primitive — "6 characters" — ahead of any helper text.
- **Disabled is `aria-disabled` plus `readOnly`, inherited from Field** — The system rule, and the text field's consequence with it: the value still submits.
- **Proposed primitive: `getPinInputProps`** — No primitive exists yet. The proposal filters input to the character set, uppercases alphanumeric codes, caps at `length`, reports completion once per fill, and derives each drawn box's state — filled, active, empty — from the value and the selection, so the boxes cannot disagree with the input.
- **Web and native** — Web: one `<input>` with `inputmode="numeric"` (or `text` for alphanumeric), `autocomplete="one-time-code"` or `off`, `type="password"` for `pin`, `maxLength`, inside a Field; the boxes are `aria-hidden` and the input lies over them, transparent, so taps anywhere land in it. React Native: one `TextInput` with `keyboardType="number-pad"`, `textContentType="oneTimeCode"` on iOS and `autoComplete="sms-otp"` on Android — the two platforms' SMS autofill hooks — and `secureTextEntry` for `pin`; the boxes are `View`s with `accessibilityElementsHidden` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"`, so only the input is announced. `name` is web-only. Rata-drawn around the OS text input (decision N5): the single `TextInput` is the platform's, so SMS autofill, paste and deletion are too; the boxes are drawn from the recipe. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

### `label`

```ts
label: ReactNode
```

What the code is. Always required — `labelHidden` hides it, nothing removes it.

**Use when**

- Where the code came from, when that is the useful part: "Code from your authenticator app".

**Don't use for**

- Leaving it off because the boxes look self-explanatory. A screen reader hears one text field and nothing else.

**Accessibility** Bound to the single input by Field, so it is the accessible name. The boxes are `aria-hidden` and add nothing to it.

### `length`

```ts
length: number
```

How many characters the code has. Draws that many boxes and caps the input.

**Use when**

- The exact length the server sends — usually 6 for a one-time code, 4 to 8 for a PIN.

**Don't use for**

- A variable-length code. The boxes promise a length; if it varies, use a `TextField` with `autoComplete="one-time-code"`.

**Accessibility** Becomes the input's `maxLength`, and is stated in the description chain as "6 characters" so a reader who cannot see the boxes knows how many to type.

### `value`

```ts
value?: string
```

Controls the code from outside.

**Use when**

- Clearing the field after a failed attempt.

**Don't use for**

- Passing it alongside `defaultValue`. One of them owns the state.

**Conflicts with** `defaultValue`

### `defaultValue`

```ts
defaultValue?: string = ""
```

The starting text when the component owns the state.

**Use when**

- Almost never. A pre-filled one-time code is a code someone else already read.

**Conflicts with** `value`

### `onValueChange`

```ts
onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
```

Fires with the whole code on every change.

**Use when**

- Tracking a partial code, to enable a submit button only when it is complete.

### `onComplete`

```ts
onComplete?: (value: string) => void
```

Fires once when the code reaches `length` characters.

**Use when**

- Starting verification — the commonest reason for this component's existence is to save the reader a tap.

**Don't use for**

- Navigating away inside it before the server answers. A mistyped code then becomes a page change the reader cannot undo; verify, and keep them on the field until it passes.

### `characters`

```ts
characters?: PinInputCharacters = "numeric"
```

Which characters are accepted, and which on-screen keyboard appears.

**Use when**

- `alphanumeric` for codes like recovery keys that mix letters and digits.

**Don't use for**

- Assuming lowercase. Alphanumeric codes are uppercased as typed, since case-sensitive one-time codes are a usability bug on the issuing side.

**Accessibility** Characters outside the set are dropped rather than rejected with an error, and a paste is filtered the same way — so a pasted "123-456" becomes "123456".

### `purpose`

```ts
purpose?: PinInputPurpose = "one-time-code"
```

Whether this is a code the reader was sent or a secret they know.

**Use when**

- `one-time-code` for SMS and email codes — the browser and the OS offer to fill it from the message.
- `pin` for a secret the reader remembers, which masks every box and turns autofill off.

**Don't use for**

- `one-time-code` for a PIN. It would show the secret on screen and invite the OS to suggest a code from the last SMS.

**Accessibility** `pin` renders the input as `type="password"`, so a screen reader says "bullet" rather than reading the digits aloud.

name?: string

**Use when**

- A native form post.

## Use cases

### A code sent by SMS or email

Verifying a phone number or a sign-in.

```tsx
<PinInput
  label="Verification code"
  description="We sent it to the number ending 0142."
  length={6}
  onComplete={verify}
/>
```

`purpose` defaults to `one-time-code`, which is what lets iOS, Android and the browser offer to fill it from the message — one tap instead of six.

### A wrong code

The server rejected the code the reader entered.

```tsx
<PinInput
  label="Verification code"
  length={6}
  value={code}
  onValueChange={setCode}
  status="invalid"
  message="That code did not match. Check the latest message and try again."
/>
```

Clear `code` when setting the error, and keep focus on the field. The ring is on every box, because the code is wrong as a whole.

### A PIN the reader knows

Confirming a payment or unlocking a vault with a memorised secret.

```tsx
<PinInput label="PIN" length={4} purpose="pin" />
```

`pin` masks, uses a password input and turns autofill off. The visible-and-fillable defaults are right for a code someone was sent and wrong for a secret.

### Reaching for the wrong component

A recovery key of 24 characters in groups.

```tsx
<PinInput label="Recovery key" length={24} characters="alphanumeric" />
```

Don't. Twenty-four boxes do not fit a phone and nobody types a key that long one box at a time. It is a `TextField` the reader pastes into.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<PinInput label="PIN" length={4} purpose="pin" />
```

## Token recipe

### base

A row of boxes, each the text field's box in miniature. Field owns the label, helper text, message and disabled dimming.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| gap between boxes | `space.gap.sm` |
| box inline-size | `size.control.md at md, size.control.lg at lg — a control step used as a width, the way Dialog measures itself in controls` |
| box block-size | `size.control.lg at md, calc(size.control.lg plus space.2) at lg` |
| box background | `theme.bg.surface` |
| box border | `border.default solid theme.border.strong` |
| box border-radius | `radius.element` |
| character font-family | `font.family.mono — every character the same width, so a 1 and an 8 sit centred alike` |
| character font-size | `type.control.size.lg` |
| character colour | `theme.fg.primary` |
| masked character | `a dot of space.2 in theme.fg.primary with radius.pill — a spacing step for a mark rather than a glyph, the reasoning Switch's thumb follows` |
| active box | `focus.ring-width solid theme.fg.primary at space.0 offset, on the box at the caret while the input is focused — the text field's focus departure, so this reads as a text box` |
| caret | `border.2 in theme.fg.primary, centred in the active empty box, blinking at motion.duration.slow and steady under prefers-reduced-motion` |
| validating ring | `theme.accent-role.ring on every box` |
| valid ring | `theme.success-role.ring on every box` |
| invalid ring | `theme.danger-role.ring on every box — the code is wrong as a whole, not one digit of it` |
